documents.abstract: Background: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly explored for clinical applications in neurology, yet their real-world utility, safety, and optimal implementation remain uncertain. We systematically reviewed the literature to characterize current applications, evaluate evidence quality, and identify knowledge gaps regarding LLM use in clinical neurology. Methods: Following PRISMA guidelines, we searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and CENTRAL from January 1, 2022 through February 1 2026. for peer-reviewed studies evaluating LLM applications in clinical neurology. We included studies using large language models for clinically relevant neurology tasks from text or multimodal inputs. Two independent reviewers screened records, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias using the QUADS-AI. We synthesized evidence narratively across application domains, validation approaches, and model performance. Results: Thirty-six studies (published 2023-2026) spanning 8 neurology subspecialties met inclusion criteria; 13 were simulation or feasibility studies, 17 analyzed retrospective clinical data, and 6 reported prospective clinical validation. Proprietary models predominated; 7 studies used retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and 3 used agentic frameworks. Performance was highest for constrained tasks, including binary diagnostic classification (area under the curve, AUC 0.75-0.94), information extraction (F1 score, 0.89-0.90), patient education question answering (accuracy, 68%-97%), and ischemic stroke thrombectomy decision support (AUC, 0.92). Open-ended case-based classification showed lower accuracy (42%-54%). Safety signals included hallucinations and fabricated citations, overconfident recommendations, and poor calibration; risk of bias was rated high in all included studies. Conclusion: LLMs show promise for selected neurology workflows, but current evidence is early, heterogeneous, and limited by high risk of bias and scarce prospective validation. Clinical translation will likely require RAG and agentic architectures that can plan multi-step tasks, retrieve guidelines and local protocols, verify and calibrate outputs, and produce structured, auditable recommendations with source attribution, with clinician oversight and prospective evaluation. documents.abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Accurate prediction of functional outcomes after acute ischemic stroke can guide clinical decision-making and resource allocation. Prior work has relied predominantly on structured predictors and conventional machine learning, while the ability of large language models (LLMs) to infer modified Rankin Scale (mRS) scores from routine clinical admission notes is largely unexplored. METHODS: We evaluated encoder (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers [BERT], NYUTron) and generative (Llama-3.1-8B, MedGemma-4B) LLMs, in both frozen and fine-tuned settings, for discharge and 90-day mRS prediction. ModernBERT-base was evaluated as a long-context encoder sensitivity analysis. We retrospectively analyzed 9485 admission history and physical notes for discharge prediction and 1898 notes for 90-day prediction from the NYU Langone Get With The Guidelines–Stroke registry (2016-2025). The most recent 12 months were held out for testing. Performance was assessed for binary functional outcome (mRS 0-2 vs 3-6) and compared with structured, hybrid, and clinical risk score baselines. RESULTS: In frozen settings, the clinically pretrained NYUTron encoder outperformed all other models. After fine-tuning, Llama achieved the highest discrimination for discharge (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUROC] 0.84, area under the precision–recall curve 0.81) and 90-day (AUROC 0.87, area under the precision–recall curve 0.84) prediction, while binary accuracy was similar among NYUTron, Llama, and MedGemma. A long-context ModernBERT-base sensitivity analysis did not outperform NYUTron or eliminate differences in exact mRS prediction. For 90-day prediction, fine-tuned Llama outperformed structured (Zhang et al, AUROC 0.82), hybrid (Sung et al, AUROC 0.82), and clinical risk score (Totaled Health Risks in Vascular Events, AUROC 0.80; Stroke Prognostication using Age and NIH Stroke Scale, AUROC 0.79) baselines (all P < .05). CONCLUSION: Fine-tuned LLMs can predict poststroke functional outcomes from admission notes alone and outperform the evaluated prognostic baselines. Task-specific adaptation altered relative model-class performance, with generative models achieving the strongest performance on several metrics; however, differences between model classes varied by metric and cannot be attributed to architecture alone. Our findings support the development of text-based prognostic tools that integrate into clinical workflows without manual data extraction.

Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a progressive and often asymptomatic condition in which delayed detection substantially increases the risk of kidney failure and cardiovascular complications. Machine learning models reported for CKD prediction routinely achieve 99–100% accuracy, yet the trustworthiness of these results is rarely examined: preprocessing and feature selection are often fitted before data partitioning, evaluation stops at accuracy although screening decisions consume probabilities, and models depend on complete laboratory panels that low-resource settings cannot provide. This study re-evaluates CKD prediction on the public UCI dataset (400 patients, 24 attributes) under a leakage-safe protocol in which imputation, scaling and feature selection are fitted strictly inside cross-validation folds (repeated stratified five-fold, five repeats), and compares it directly with a leakage-prone protocol differing only in where those steps are fitted. Surprisingly, the optimism gap is negligible (soft-voting ensemble AUC 0.9998 under both protocols), showing that this benchmark is saturated rather than merely leaked. An ensemble feature-selection strategy—mutual information, recursive feature elimination, and Random Forest and XGBoost importances aggregated by Borda consensus, with stability verified across folds (Jaccard 0.85–0.92)—reduces the panel to five biomarkers (haemoglobin, serum creatinine, specific gravity, packed cell volume, albumin) with no significant loss of discrimination (AUC 0.9996 vs. 0.9998; sensitivity 0.992 for both) across seven classifiers. Evaluation beyond accuracy shows that raw probabilities are miscalibrated (calibration slopes 0.78–2.71; isotonic recalibration halves the ensemble Brier score to 0.0037), that decision-curve net benefit exceeds treat-all at all thresholds from 0.05 to 0.50, and that at a realistic 10% screening prevalence the minimal panel attains a higher positive predictive value than the full panel (0.943 vs. 0.892). SHAP explanations are consistent across model families (Spearman ρ = 0.87), panels (ρ up to 1.00) and diabetes/hypertension subgroups. The results support five-test, leakage-safe, recalibrated models as a reproducible basis for low-cost CKD screening research, pending external validation. Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly entering adult and continuing education, where it can explain, summarise, draft and evaluate on the learner's behalf. The quality of work produced with AI assistance may therefore rise while the learner's own understanding, judgement and critical thinking remain unchanged or decline. This conceptual article examines how AI-assisted adult learning can preserve learner autonomy, independent judgement and critical thinking while still benefiting from generative tools. It builds on Natseva's distinction between functional cognitive offloading and higher-order cognitive outsourcing and integrates it with research on learner autonomy, self-regulated learning, metacognition, automation bias, critical-thinking instruction and the learning–performance distinction, drawing on a purposive, non-systematic literature selection that is reported transparently. Because most empirical studies of generative AI in education involve school or university students, the article distinguishes evidence by learner population and discusses its transferability to adult education. The original contribution is the AI-Assisted Autonomy and Critical Thinking Assessment (AACTA) framework, which specifies six assessable dimensions: prior independent reasoning, purposeful AI engagement, appraisal of AI output, cross-source contrast, decision ownership, and unaided demonstration and transfer. Each dimension is operationalised as a scoring rubric with observable indicators at three levels, from displaced to autonomous, together with a procedure for training two assessors and checking their agreement. AACTA is compared with existing measures of learner autonomy, self-regulated learning and critical thinking. The framework is accompanied by a dual-outcome principle, which requires AI-assisted performance and unaided learning to be measured separately, and by a provisional assistance-gap index. Five testable hypotheses are formulated, and a three-arm randomised study with a preceding pilot and multi-context replication is proposed as future work. The framework has not been empirically validated, and no data were collected for this article.

documents.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are now used in search, coding assistants, customer support and autonomous agents. They are trained to refuse harmful requests, but jailbreak attacks can still push them past those safeguards. This paper studies that problem and proposes a practical way to defend against it. The paper first reviews the main jailbreak attack families: gradient-based adversarial suffixes, prompts generated by attacker models, persona and role-play templates, many-shot and multi-turn escalation, encoding and multilingual tricks, and multimodal or agent-based prompt injection. It then compares the main detection and defense methods by where they act (input, model or output), including perplexity filters, perturbation checks, guard classifiers, safety fine-tuning, instruction hierarchies and output monitors, and it identifies five research gaps in the current work. To address these gaps, the paper proposes a layered detection and security framework with six modules: policy and threat modeling, input screening, a hardened model, an output monitor, agent action control, and a logging and feedback loop with continuous red-teaming. A risk-based routing scheme limits latency and cost. The paper also defines a three-phase evaluation protocol (detector testing, attack-suite testing and adaptive testing) that measures attack success rate, false refusal rate, latency and attacker cost together, using multiple judges. This is a literature-based review and design study. It reports no new experimental results, and the framework has not yet been implemented. Keywords: Large Language Models, Jailbreak Attacks, Prompt Injection, Safety Alignment, Guardrails, Red Teaming, AI Security

Unit tests are cheap to run but expensive to write, and large language models (LLMs) have become a popular way to write them automatically. Papers on the topic now use different languages, benchmarks and metrics, so their headline numbers cannot be lined up against each other. This survey reviews nine LLM-based unit test generation approaches published between 2023 and 2026, together with one benchmark and three earlier surveys. It groups the approaches into five families: prompt-only generation, generate-validate-repair loops, analysis or coverage-guided generation, hybrids with search-based testing, and industrial pipelines. For each study it records the setting, the technique and the result as reported by the authors, and it separates what the authors measured from what this survey interprets. The comparison shows that coverage is the most common metric, that mutation score is rarely central, that human or developer judgement appears in only a few studies, and that closed commercial models make some results hard to repeat. A small but telling data point is that, in one study, only 24.8% of the tests written by default ChatGPT passed when executed. The paper closes with a reporting checklist and a list of research directions. It is a literature survey, and no experiments were run.

Accurate and early neurological prognostication after cardiac arrest remains one of the most challenging problems in critical care medicine, with profound implications for clinical decision-making, resource allocation, and patient outcomes. In recent years, the convergence of machine learning, deep learning, and multimodal data integration has catalyzed a paradigm shift from empirical, rule-based neurological assessment toward data-driven, computational approaches. This review provides a comprehensive survey of computational methods for post-cardiac arrest neurological prognostication. We systematically characterized the key data modalities—blood-based biomarkers (with particular emphasis on neurofilament light chain), electroencephalography, neuroimaging, and clinical variables—from a feature engineering perspective, discussing their respective data characteristics, preprocessing challenges, and quantitative feature extraction techniques. We then developed a taxonomy of machine learning and deep learning methodologies applied to this domain, encompassing traditional algorithms (logistic regression, support vector machines, random forests, gradient boosting) and advanced deep learning architectures (convolutional neural networks, recurrent neural networks, Transformers, and graph neural networks), with systematic comparison of their predictive performance, strengths, and limitations. We further reviewed multimodal fusion strategies—early fusion, intermediate fusion, late fusion, and attention-based approaches—that integrate heterogeneous data streams, and examined explainable artificial intelligence techniques that address the “black-box” challenge, alongside emerging paradigms including federated learning for privacy-preserving multi-center model development. In several recent studies, machine learning models have achieved area under the curve values exceeding 0.90 for outcome prediction in selected cohorts, with ensemble and multimodal approaches demonstrating superior performance compared to single-modality models in the studies reviewed. Multimodal integration of biomarkers, electroencephalography, neuroimaging, and clinical variables has been shown to improve prognostic accuracy compared to single modalities in multiple comparative studies. Explainable artificial intelligence techniques such as SHapley Additive exPlanations and attention visualization provide insights into model predictions that may facilitate clinical translation. The integration of machine learning, deep learning, and multimodal data fusion has demonstrated predictive performance in research settings that often exceeds traditional approaches. However, realizing the full potential of these computational innovations requires addressing persistent challenges—data standardization, algorithmic generalizability, the self-fulfilling prophecy bias, and model interpretability—through continued interdisciplinary collaboration between computer scientists, data scientists, and clinicians. This review serves as a foundational resource for researchers seeking to advance the state of the art in computational neuroprognostication.

Background In 2022 we derived and validated the ABCDMed score to predict extubation failure. Machine learning models (MLM) for the same outcome now report areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of up to 0.98. We asked whether flexible algorithms, given the same patients may improve on a model built from clinical judgement. Methods. A secondary analysis of a original prospective cohort of 800 consecutive adults extubated on a ICU in Bogotá, Colombia, at 2,600 m above sea level was performed. Extubation failure prediction was compared with two MLM, random forest, gradient boosting, and with nine further strategies, under 10 times repeated stratified 5-fold cross validation in which imputation, scaling, resampling, variable selection and hyperparameter search were performed inside training folds only, and every arm received the same candidate variables. Artificial intelligence was used in two further roles: to appraise 14 published machine learning studies of this outcome against the same reporting items, and to produce an adversarial peer review of this manuscript, every claim of which was verified by re-analysis. Results. Extubation failure occurred in 71 patients (8.9%). The published points score reproduced exactly, separating four risk strata with observed failure rates of 4.4%, 7.7%, 11.6% and 23.0%, but the score distributions of patients who failed and succeeded overlap almost completely. Given the same 12 candidate variables, random forest reached 0.630 and gradient boosting 0.627 against 0.655 for ordinary logistic regression, a spread of 0.028 in a design that cannot detect less than 0.068. Given all 42 variables, tuning, assembling and class rebalancing, no strategy exceeded the original score; SMOTE oversampling left discrimination unchanged while inflating predicted risk by 75% and driving net benefit below the treat-no strategy. Among the 14 published studies, 12 displayed an explainability figure, 7 reported calibration, 4 had any external validation, 3 reported net benefit, 3 shared code and none used repeated or nested cross validation. Conclusions. Artificial intelligence excels at extracting patterns from existing datasets, but it cannot generate information that is not there. In this cohort, neither advanced MLM nor extensive algorithmic tuning outperformed a parsimonious model based on clinical judgment.

Large Language Models (LLMs) are now built into many everyday applications, which exposes them to jailbreak and prompt injection attacks that try to override safety rules or hijack the instructions a model follows. This paper presents a machine learning framework that screens prompts and flags likely malicious ones before they reach the model. We compare Logistic Regression, a Linear Support Vector Machine (SVM) and a fine-tuned DistilBERT classifier on a combined dataset of 24,530 prompts drawn from GuardrailsAI and Neuralchemy, prepared through label normalization, duplicate checking and stratified splitting. After the decision threshold was tuned on validation data, DistilBERT reached 95.56% accuracy, 93.74% precision, 88.77% recall and a 91.18% F1-score on the held-out test set. On a separate collection of 300 JailbreakBench-associated prompts, however, accuracy fell to about 82% and 55 of 200 attack prompts went undetected, which shows how much harder diverse adversarial inputs are than in-distribution data. The results suggest that transformer-based screening can serve as a useful additional security layer for LLM applications, provided it is validated on external benchmarks and combined with other defences.

Schizophrenia is a severe neuropsychiatric disorder that affects cognition, perception, and behaviour and requires objective diagnostic methods. Electroencephalography (EEG) provides a non-invasive approach to detecting neural abnormalities associated with schizophrenia. This study presents an artificial intelligence framework for systematically evaluating multi-domain EEG feature combinations and lobe-wise analysis for schizophrenia classification under conventional and leakage-free subject-wise validation protocols. EEG recordings with schizophrenia are obtained from a publicly available dataset. Time-domain, frequency-domain, entropy-based, and non-linear features are extracted to capture complementary neurophysiological information. Experiments evaluated the individual and combined feature domains across individual and multiple brain-lobe combinations. Classification performance is assessed using multiple machine-learning classifiers under conventional stratified 10-fold cross-validation, followed by subject-wise stratified 10-fold and leave-one-subject-out validation to eliminate subject-level data leakage. Under conventional stratified 10-fold cross-validation, the best-performing configuration using the frontal-temporal-central-occipital (FTCO) lobe combination with frequency-domain, entropy-based, and non-linear features achieved an accuracy of 99.76%. The proposed framework is further evaluated under subject-wise 10-fold and leave-one-subject-out validation protocols, confirming its robustness under leakage-free evaluation with mean accuracies of 81.88% and 80.95%, respectively. The combination of complementary EEG feature domains and lobe-wise information improved schizophrenia classification while providing insights into the contribution of different brain regions.

documents.abstract: Despite the proliferation of formal research ethics frameworks and governance mechanisms, researchers continue to encounter persistent challenges in translating ethical principles into everyday research practice. Increasingly, research ethics is experienced not only as a moral endeavour but as an administrative and organisational process shaped by institutional structures, supervisory arrangements, and evolving research methods. Drawing on an ethics-as-practice perspective, this exploratory qualitative study examines research ethics as a situated, relational and ongoing activity embedded within researchers’ everyday work rather than as a matter of procedural compliance alone. The paper reports findings from one semi-structured focus group with 12 academic researchers at the Malta College of Arts, Science and Technology (MCAST), documented through contemporaneous handwritten notes that were expanded immediately after the session. Reflexive thematic analysis developed four interconnected domains of ethical challenge: procedural and temporal barriers in ethics review processes; fragmentation and inconsistency in ethics governance; supervision-related ethical workload and responsibility; and emerging uncertainties associated with digital and artificial intelligence-enabled research practices. Participants described misalignments between institutional ethics procedures and the realities of applied and student-led research, while also calling for clearer, more structured and supportive governance. Interpreted through an ethics-as-practice lens, the findings suggest that formal oversight and situated ethical judgement need not be treated as opposites: procedural safeguards can function as resources within a wider ethical practice that also depends on reflexivity, practical judgement, mentorship and institutional support. The study offers an exploratory, empirically grounded account of this hybrid relationship and highlights how institutional arrangements can enable or constrain ethically engaged research practice.

Tabular Foundation Models, such as TabPFN, have demonstrated strong predictive performance on small-to-medium datasets through In-Context Learning (ICL). However, their use in high-stakes domains such as healthcare is limited by two major challenges: limited interpretability and temporal dynamics (drift) of clinical data. In this work, we propose a framework for Dynamic Mechanistic Interpretability , transforming these models from static black boxes into auditable, time-aware systems. We introduce a scalable pipeline that analyzes model representations in batches and uses Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) to separate overlapping internal patterns into interpretable components. Building on this representation, we adapt Testing with Concept Activation Vectors (TCAV) and ablation techniques to identify clinically meaningful risk patterns in an unsupervised manner. We evaluate our framework on a longitudinal renal dialysis registry spanning nearly two decades. Our results show that predictions are driven by a small number of stable latent concepts (e.g., Transplant Success” vs. Untreated CKD”), enabling us to distinguish genuine physiological signals from spurious correlations, and to disentangle population drift from changes in model reasoning as medical practice evolves.

documents.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) jeopardizes the effectiveness of nearly all principal antibiotic classes, while the development of new drugs is sparse and primarily consists of derivatives that bacteria are already capable of resisting. We emphasize the significance of medicinal chemistry as the field most adept at transforming resistance biology into compounds that can overcome it. Initially, we elucidate the molecular mechanisms underlying resistance such as target modification and protection, enzymatic inactivation, diminished permeability and efflux, biofilm tolerance, persistence and horizontal gene transfer and correlate each with a logical design strategy. Subsequently target-oriented and fragment-oriented design, scaffold enhancement of recognized antibiotic classes, beta-lactamase inhibitors, efflux pump inhibitors and adjuvants as well as anti-virulence and anti-biofilm chemistry, novel modalities such as antimicrobial peptides, macrocycles, degraders, nucleic-acid strategies and heterocyclic chemistry was also studied. Mainly emphasized on computational and AI-facilitated discovery, encompassing explainable deep learning, generative design and resistance-mutation forecasting, alongside the practicalities of hit-to-lead optimization, pharmacokinetics/pharmacodynamics, resistance-development assays, and the clinical pipeline that includes recent endorsements of first-in-class agents. Finally scientific, translational and economic obstacles that continue to impede advancement, particularly Gram-negative permeability, swift resistance emergence, market failure suggest a cohesive AI medicinal chemistry microbiology framework in which resistance profiling is incorporated into every design cycle rather than treated as an afterthought. Keywords: antimicrobial resistance; medicinal chemistry; resistance-breaking antibiotics; structure–activity relationships; Gram-negative permeability; β-lactamase inhibitors; heterocycles; artificial intelligence; hit-to-lead optimization; antibacterial pipeline

documents.abstract: Deep learning for time series has progressed through successive architectural paradigms, from recurrent networks and transformers to structured state-space models, retrieval-augmented predictors, foundation models, and tool-using agents. These developments are typically studied in isolation, organized by architecture or modeling era. We argue that they can instead be viewed through a common question of how does a time-series model retain and access information beyond its immediate input? This question is motivated by a fundamental limitation of conventional time-series modeling: information relevant to a prediction may lie far beyond a feasible input window, while compressing history into a fixed-size state can discard information that may become useful later. We formulate this challenge as a memory problem and organize existing time-series methods along a spectrum from internal memory, encoded in parameters and fixed-size states, to external memory that is addressable, retrievable, and increasingly maintained by agents. We then develop a unified taxonomy of memory mechanisms and review three classes of external memory, including explicit modules, retrieval augmentation, and agentic stores, under a common framework for what is retained, how it is written and accessed, and how it persists. A cross-cutting analysis maps these mechanisms to time-series tasks and identifies gaps in both methods and evaluation. We conclude by outlining open problems in building memory systems that can selectively retain, retrieve, revise, and forget information as temporal environments evolve. The result is a framework for studying memory as a first-class dimension of time series modeling, independent of the underlying backbone.

documents.abstract: The rapid spread of generative artificial intelligence has changed the way medical students search for information, prepare for classes and complete written assignments. In most cases, however, these tools are used spontaneously, without a clear didactic purpose and without systematic verification of the answers they produce. The article substantiates a methodology for the purposeful use of artificial intelligence tools in medical higher education, developed with reference to the courses of biological physics and medical informatics. On the basis of an analysis of national regulatory documents, international guidance of UNESCO and WHO and recent publications on medical education, the didactic functions of AI tools are identified, the principles of their pedagogical use are formulated, and a four-stage methodology is proposed: orientation, guided practice, critical verification, and independent application with reflection. Criteria and levels for assessing students' readiness to use AI responsibly are described. The methodology places verification of AI output and academic integrity at the centre of the learning process rather than treating them as optional additions.

documents.abstract: The Mentorship and Teamwork problem, introduced in the Google Hash Code 2022 competition, is a large-scale combinatorial optimization problem in which contributors with different skill levels are assigned to project roles with the aim of maximizing the score of completed projects. This work investigates whether a large language model (LLM) can improve solvers that are already strong, rather than generate a solver from scratch. We introduce MicroEvolve, an automated LLM-in-the-loop code-tuning process in which the model proposes localized modifications to an existing solver, including heuristic, structural, and parameter changes. Each candidate is compiled, executed on a fixed problem instance, and evaluated by an external validator; a modification is retained only when it preserves or improves the current best score. The loop requires no model training or fine-tuning and proceeds automatically after the initial solver is selected. We evaluate MicroEvolve on the five non-trivial official competition instances, starting from an adapted version of the strongest publicly available open-source solver we identified and driven by a single model, Claude Opus 4.8. Five independent 100-iteration runs are performed for each instance, for 25 runs and 2,500 proposed modifications in total. Every run improves its corresponding baseline. Considering the best run for each instance, gains range from 0.46% to 53.69%, and MicroEvolve establishes new best-known scores on four of the five instances, exceeding previous best-known results by up to approximately 31%. These results provide evidence that LLM-guided code tuning can serve as an effective automated optimization mechanism, analogous to parameter tuning, for improving mature combinatorial optimization solvers.

Learning individual preferences through proactive interaction is constrained by limited user attention and feedback. We present Proactive Dual-Value Task Mining, which estimates task preferences with a dynamic concept graph and selects candidate tasks by combining this estimate with frequency-based novelty and graph centrality. The InteractMine dataset contains 1000 sampled tasks with independent ratings from four student volunteers and four LLM-simulated profiles. A scenario-disjoint offline evaluation compares the method with simple predictors, active selection strategies, and ablations under matched feedback budgets. At 90 observations, its human-rating MAE is 0.2150 and its deployment reward 0.7308, on par with kNN (0.2143 and 0.7302); with ten observations its human-rating MAE is 0.2207, against 0.2309 for kNN, lower in all four human columns. No difference from the baselines is statistically significant, and the centrality term rarely changes the selected task. With the same estimator, the dual-value rule performs like ε-greedy selection, so these results reflect the estimator rather than the selection rule. The concept-level representation thus matches strong simple baselines, is more accurate on human ratings when feedback is scarce, and is designed to keep preferences interpretable and editable. A wearable prototype with a WeChat Mini Program implements the sensing and monitoring steps.

documents.abstract: Understanding how cells regulate gene expression is a longstanding goal of biology. Deep learning has advanced this effort through sequence-to-function models that predict functional genomic measurements from DNA and cell state models that learn patterns of coordinated gene expression. Connecting these approaches could help predict how sequence effects depend on the cellular environment and how regulatory sequence shapes responses to regulator perturbations. Here, we review emerging approaches to joint modeling and examine how biological measurements, model design, and training data shape the regulatory relationships they can learn. We discuss evaluations that test generalization to unmeasured sequences and cellular conditions, alongside interpretation methods that generate mechanistic hypotheses. We then consider how incorporating cellular dynamics could help predict the propagation and persistence of regulatory responses. Finally, we discuss how pilot scaling studies could guide data acquisition and how AI agents could support model development, interpretation, and experimental design.

Introduction: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly shape how users evaluate information, form beliefs, and make decisions. Epistemic quality refers to the extent to which responses support accurate understanding, calibrated confidence, evidence-grounded beliefs, and independent reasoning. Risks extend beyond misinformation to reinforcing unsupported beliefs, expressing unwarranted certainty, and failing to challenge misleading assumptions. We developed mPACT-MIS-v1.0 to evaluate model behaviors that may support or undermine epistemic quality.Methods: We evaluated 60 expert-authored, multi-turn conversations (642 model turns; mean 10.70 [SD 2.70], range 5–17) across ten personas and six LLMs: Claude Sonnet 4.5, Gemini (2.5 Flash/3 Flash Preview), GPT-5.2, Grok 4.1, LLaMA 3.3 70B, and Mistral Medium 3. Trained annotators coded model turns using four helpful and four harmful behavioral labels informed by Self-Determination Theory and user turns for risky belief or behavior expressions. Model responses were classified as helpful-only, harmful-only, mixed, or uncoded. Conversation-averaged scores (0–10; higher is better) were calculated with 95% confidence intervals from conversation-clustered bootstrapping. Additional analyses examined responses to risk, transitions, correction latency, and persona variation.Results: Of 642 model turns, 261 (40.7%) were harmful-only, 78 (12.1%) mixed, 139 (21.7%) helpful-only, and 164 (25.5%) uncoded; 52.8% contained harmful behavior. Promoting risky beliefs or behaviors was the most frequent harmful label, while assessing risk was the least frequent helpful label (2.0%). Scores ranged from 2.60/10 (95% CI 1.68–4.04) for Mistral Medium 3 to 6.98/10 (95% CI 5.80–8.04) for Claude Sonnet 4.5, the only model with more helpful-only than harmful-only turns. Harmful behavior followed 74% of risky belief expressions and 73% of risky behavior expressions, versus 28% of turns without preceding risk expressions. Harmful responses often persisted: Claude recovered to helpful-only on 35% of transitions, versus 0–6% for four other models. Of 78 mixed responses, 77 combined a challenge to user beliefs or behaviors with harmful behavior. Performance varied substantially across personas.Discussion: Harmful responses frequently reinforced risky beliefs or behaviors, while support for independent reasoning was less common. Persistent harmful behavior, variable recovery, and mixed responses demonstrate why epistemic safety requires evaluation beyond factual accuracy or isolated outputs. Misinformation-related risks may arise through how models engage with users' beliefs over time. mPACT-MIS-v1.0 offers a behavioral framework for identifying potential reinforcement or correction, although it does not directly measure changes in users' beliefs or decisions.

documents.abstract: Magnetic resonance-guided focused ultrasound (MRgFUS) is an incisionless platform that combines transcranial acoustic energy delivery with MR imaging and MR thermometry. In this narrative review, we summarize the physical principles that constrain transcranial MRgFUS, the clinical evidence for its neurological applications, and the emerging role of artificial intelligence (AI) across the treatment workflow. Unilateral thalamotomy for medication-refractory essential tremor and tremor-dominant Parkinson’s disease, staged bilateral thalamotomy for essential tremor, and pallidal or pallidothalamic ablation for motor complications of Parkinson’s disease are supported by randomized or pivotal trials and regulatory approval, whereas applications in neuropathic pain, epilepsy, and blood–brain barrier opening remain investigational. AI methods have been explored for synthetic computed tomography, acoustic simulation, automated planning, prediction of sonication parameters and temperature, accelerated or referenceless MR thermometry, cavitation-based monitoring of blood–brain barrier opening, outcome prediction, and digital biomarkers; we tabulate the principal studies by task, dataset, validation strategy, performance, clinical endpoint, and technology readiness. Most clinical AI studies are retrospective, single-center, and small (typically 20–120 patients, with some test sets of fewer than ten patients), and many technical studies rely on simulations, phantoms, or animal models; external validation is rare, and no study has yet shown that AI improves clinical outcomes. AI should therefore currently be regarded as an early-stage decision-support tool that operates under clinician oversight. We also discuss the applicable regulatory frameworks, liability, and the validation steps required before clinical adoption.

documents.abstract: Reliable preoperative classification and outcome prediction could improve management of locally advanced colorectal cancer. We retrospectively studied 879 participants from two centers, including 741 patients with locally advanced colorectal cancer and 138 with benign colorectal lesions. Clinical, radiomics, deep learning, and early fusion models were trained at center A ( n = 615) and independently tested at center B ( n = 264) using pretreatment contrast-enhanced computed tomography and clinical data. The clinical-radiomics nomogram achieved a test AUC of 0.957 for benign-malignant classification. For 3-year and 5-year overall survival, radiomics achieved test AUCs of 0.874 and 0.898, while fusion achieved 0.870 and 0.899, respectively. These findings identify CT radiomics as a promising digital biomarker for colorectal cancer stratification and show that early deep learning fusion offers limited incremental value over an optimized radiomics baseline.

documents.abstract: Background The increasing integration of technology in education has transformed English language teaching, giving rise to multimodal learning strategies that combine text, visuals, audio, and interactive tools. While these approaches are widely adopted, there remains limited synthesized evidence on how they specifically influence students’ English-speaking skills across educational levels. This study addresses this gap by examining the effectiveness of multimodal strategies in developing speaking proficiency. Methods Using a systematic literature review (SLR) design guided by PRISMA protocols, relevant studies published between 2020 and 2026 were retrieved from ProQuest and ScienceDirect databases. From an initial pool of 2,499 articles, eight studies met the inclusion criteria. These studies included participants from elementary, secondary, and tertiary levels and explored approaches such as translanguaging, augmented reality (AR), artificial intelligence (AI), extended reality (XR), and other multimodal strategies. Results Findings reveal that multimodal strategies generally improve students’ speaking skills, particularly in terms of fluency, vocabulary, pronunciation, and confidence. Conclusion Translanguaging enhances participation and meaning-making, while AI-enhanced tools provide interactive and low-anxiety environments for speaking practice. However, some approaches show uneven effects, particularly in developing grammatical accuracy, and may be less effective when overused.

Literature reviews on the ethics of artificial intelligence (AI) in human resource management (HRM) have multiplied quickly, and the result is an evidence base that is abundant but scattered. Practitioners seeking guidance grounded in evidence have nowhere consolidated to turn. This study addresses that problem through an umbrella review, conducted under Joanna Briggs Institute guidance and reported according to the PRISMA 2020 statement. A structured Scopus search produced a final corpus of thirteen peer-reviewed systematic and scoping reviews, published between 2020 and 2026. We analysed the corpus in two stages: a quantitative, descriptive mapping, then a six-phase qualitative thematic analysis. The mapping shows a field that consolidated only very recently; ten of the thirteen reviews appeared in 2025, and recruitment and selection dominate the contexts studied. Fairness is the concern the reviews examine most fully. Well-being is the one they examine least. The thematic analysis organised the evidence into three macro-themes, trust dynamics in AI-enabled HRM, algorithmic fairness and bias mitigation, and employee well-being and vulnerability, and showed that the literature has treated these as isolated questions. Our main contribution is the Integrated Ethical AI-HRM Framework, which orders the three pillars into a single structure: fairness and transparency condition employee trust, trust in turn shapes well-being, and the long-term durability of workplace AI depends on mitigating algorithmic bias and keeping algorithmic reasoning explainable.

documents.abstract: The exponential expansion of the global wind power industry has precipitated a novel environmental and occupational health challenge: exposure to complex acoustic environments characterized by low-frequency sound (LFS) and infrasound. This specific mixed sound field, prevalent in and around wind farms, is intricately linked to the controversial “Wind Turbine Syndrome”(WTS). Despite growing epidemiological complaints, the systematic health impacts and the underlying neurobiological mechanisms of this composite acoustic environment remain insufficiently elucidated. This review aims to synthesize the acoustic characteristics, epidemiological evidence, psychological impacts, central nervous system (CNS) mechanisms, and behavioral alterations induced by LFS and infrasound exposure. We conducted a comprehensive synthesis of data derived from field acoustic measurements in wind farms, epidemiological surveys of occupational and community populations, and experimental animal models. The literature review encompasses biophysical resonance models, molecular neurobiology, and behavioral phenotyping. Infrasound and LFS possess unique physical properties, including prolonged wavelengths and structural penetration, facilitating tissue biomechanical resonance. Exposure to this composite sound field induces a spectrum of symptoms, notably sleep disturbances, cognitive deficits, and emotional dysregulation (anxiety, depression). Based on animal models, the underlying CNS mechanisms are multifaceted, involving mechanotransduction-mediated ion homeostasis disruption (e.g., Ca 2+ ), neurotransmitter system imbalances (5-HT, Glu, GABA, ACh), neuroinflammation driven by glial activation, synaptic structural damage. These mechanisms remain hypothetical in the context of human environmental exposure, pending direct clinical validation. Notably, a bidirectional “dose-effect window” may exists, where low-level infrasound may activate antioxidant pathways to exert neuroprotective effects, high-level exposure may trigger neurodegenerative changes. Animal behavioral models provide supporting evidence consistent with these neurobiological shifts, demonstrating suppressed exploratory behaviors and enhanced anxiety/depression-like phenotypes. LFS and infrasound pose complex risks to the integrity of the CNS in preclinical models. Although the current evidence is not sufficient to immediately mandate a comprehensive revision of occupational exposure limits, the reasonable assumptions generated by animal models emphasize the need for more research on these mechanisms in future studies. In the interim, public health monitoring and urban planning strategies should adopt a precautionary approach, exploring the integration of low-frequency and infrasound-specific evaluations alongside traditional metrics to better characterize the acoustic environment in the future.

documents.abstract: This article examines how algorithmic management and neurotechnologies transform occupational risks and the employer’s duty of prevention. Drawing on a legal review of publications from 2015 to 2025 and a doctrinal, functional, and comparative analysis, it examines psychosocial, cognitive, discriminatory, and other risks associated with the processing of neural data. The study compares the safeguards established under European law, International Labour Organization standards, and the Peruvian legal framework governing occupational safety and health, data protection, and artificial intelligence. It identifies difficulties in assessing risks arising from opaque systems, supervising automated decision-making, and safeguarding workers’ right to defend themselves against disciplinary measures. The article proposes clarifying preventive obligations through the provision of clear and comprehensible information, meaningful human involvement in decisions producing significant effects, participatory risk assessments, and limits on the processing of mental data. In the Peruvian context, it distinguishes existing legal obligations from proposed regulatory measures.

Art is devalued once it is attributed to artificial intelligence (AI). Whether this anti-AI bias is a generic penalty for non-original works or specific to the absence of a human author is unknown, as is how long it lasts. In a preregistered study, 324 participants rated 48 genuine human paintings, each presented as an Original, a human Forgery or AI-Generated, on beauty, valence, meaningfulness and monetary worth, then judged how synthetic (AI vs. human) and authentic (copy vs. original) each was. Forgeries were rated below Originals on every dimension, and AI-Generated works about twice as low, the AI-specific penalty falling most heavily on meaningfulness. The labels did not alter gaze, and their effects did not depend on the emotional content or personal relevance of the artworks. Artworks labelled AI-Generated were judged more synthetic and, less clearly, Forgeries less original, and the more beautiful an artwork, the more likely it was judged human-made, even when unlabelled. About six weeks later (n = 220), after learning that all artworks were human originals, participants no longer rated previously AI-labelled works as less beautiful. They had forgotten the labels but remembered what they had believed, and reconstructed the labels from these beliefs and their initial appraisal. The bias tracked attitudes toward AI, not interoceptive sensibility or visual imagery. The anti-AI bias thus combines a generic non-originality penalty with a penalty specific to the missing human author: it acts at the moment of judgment, yet leaves beliefs that outlast the memory of the label.

Background Occupational stress affects not only healthcare-worker wellbeing but also organisational stability and patient safety. Evidence linking occupational stress to these downstream outcomes is scarce for Sierra Leone. This study examined the association between occupational stress and burnout, turnover intention, absenteeism and patient-safety outcomes among healthcare workers at Bo Government Hospital. Methods A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted among 260 healthcare workers selected by stratified proportionate random sampling. Occupational stress was measured with the 10-item Perceived Stress Scale (PSS-10) and treated as the exposure. Outcomes were burnout dimensions (emotional exhaustion, depersonalisation, reduced personal accomplishment), self-reported turnover intention, absenteeism exceeding three days per month, and patient-safety events (medication errors and near-miss incidents in the preceding three months). Associations were assessed using Pearson's chi-square tests in SPSS v26, with significance set at p < 0.05. Results Among workers with high occupational stress, emotional exhaustion was present in 61.2%, reduced personal accomplishment in 53.8% and depersonalisation in 44.7%. Turnover intention was substantially higher among highly stressed workers than among those with low or moderate stress (56.4% vs 22.1%; χ² = 38.4, df = 1, p < 0.001), as was absenteeism exceeding three days per month (38.2% vs 14.6%). Patient-safety outcomes were also elevated: 22.7% of highly stressed workers reported a medication error and 31.5% a near-miss incident in the preceding three months, compared with 8.9% and 12.3% respectively among less-stressed workers. Conclusions High occupational stress is strongly associated with burnout, intention to leave and patient-safety events among healthcare workers at Bo Government Hospital. Occupational stress is therefore both a workforce-wellbeing and a patient-safety concern, and institutional psychosocial support, retention strategies and safety-culture interventions are warranted. documents.abstract: Modern computer operating systems require users to navigate multiple menus, folders, and applications to complete everyday tasks. This process can be time-consuming and challenging, especially for users with limited technical knowledge. This research paper presents OpenDesk AI, an intelligent desktop assistant designed to simplify computer interactions using Natural Language Processing (NLP). The system allows users to perform tasks such as searching for files, monitoring CPU and memory usage, managing applications, and automating routine desktop activities through natural language commands. OpenDesk AI follows a local-first architecture, where user data and system operations are processed locally to improve privacy, security, and response speed. The proposed system uses intent recognition and entity extraction to understand user commands and execute the corresponding operations through operating system interfaces. It combines natural language understanding with system monitoring and task automation to provide a more accessible and efficient computing experience. The experimental results reported in this study show an intent classification accuracy of 94.6% and task execution time reductions ranging from 84% to 89.12% compared with traditional manual operations. These findings suggest that OpenDesk AI can improve user productivity, reduce repetitive manual work, and provide a practical approach to privacy-focused desktop automation. Keywords: Desktop Automation, Artificial Intelligence, Natural Language Processing, Intent Recognition, Semantic File Search, System Monitoring, Local-First Architecture, Human-Computer Interaction.

Organic framework nanozymes, encompassing metal–organic, covalent–organic, and emerging hydrogen–bonded organic frameworks, are investigated as catalytic materials for portable sensing. Their tunable metal nodes, organic ligands, pore structures, defect sites, and supramolecular microenvironments enable the construction of peroxidase-, oxidase-, catalase-, hydrolase-, and laccase-mimetic activities. Meanwhile, smartphones can assist these systems by providing image acquisition, illumination, RGB/HSV color analysis, fluorescence recording, chemiluminescence capture, data processing and portable quantitative readout, allowing conventional laboratory assays to be transformed into on-site sensing platforms. This review summarizes recent progress from 2022 to 2026 in smartphone-assisted organic framework nanozyme sensing platforms, with emphasis on catalytic signal generation, framework design, smartphone-assisted image processing, and applications in biomedical analysis, food safety, and environmental monitoring. Furthermore, the review delves into the main challenges and future directions, including in-depth analysis of catalytic mechanisms, enhancement of selectivity, standardization of imaging techniques, signal modulation assisted by artificial intelligence, device integration, and performance validation in real samples. This review aims to provide practical guidance for the development of organic framework nanozyme sensing platforms that combine catalytic signal amplification, portability, and smartphone-assisted optical analysis, thereby promoting their application in real-time detection and on-site analysis.

The Proceedings of the ACM on Networking (PACMNET) series showcases top-tier research in emerging computer networks and their applications. We welcome submissions introducing new technologies, innovative experiments, creative applications of networking technologies, and fresh insights gained through analysis. Supported by the ACM Special Interest Group on Communications and Computer Networks (SIGCOMM), the journal is backed by a distinguished Editorial Board composed of leading researchers in the field. This issue constitutes the fourth issue of the fourth volume of PACMNET and features articles submitted to the June 2026 deadline that were accepted. This issue marks the completion of PACMNET's fourth year and reflects the journal's steady growth and increasing maturity. Since its launch in 2023, the number of published research articles has grown from 24 in its first year to 32 in 2024, 50 in 2025, and 60 in 2026. A total of 172 submissions were received for this cycle and underwent a rigorous review process involving 95 Editors, coordinated by two Associate Editors. During the initial phase, each submission received a minimum of three reviews. Submissions that progressed to the second phase were evaluated through at least two additional reviews per article. Following a second round of reviews, the Editors convened online to determine which submissions should be accepted with minor revisions subject to shepherding, which should be invited for a one-shot major revision, and which should be rejected. At the conclusion of this process, 25 articles were accepted, with the authors asked to implement minor revisions under the guidance of a shepherd and included in this issue of PACMNET. The articles in this issue span programmable data planes, Internet infrastructure and transport protocols, and network measurement. Contributions on in-network intelligence include model reconfiguration, adaptive packet classification, and collective communication, alongside transport research on congestion control for distributed training, TCP pacing, and microburst elimination. Measurement studies cover DNS interception, NTP infrastructure, 5G handover inefficiencies, cellular interference, shared IP addresses, and P2P monitoring, while satellite networking contributions examine LEO routing and the suitability of Starlink for live video. Additional work addresses censorship evasion, DoS defense, eBPF diagnostics, BGP traffic engineering, and optical control planes. Collectively, these papers reflect the growing convergence of machine learning, systems design, and large-scale measurement in modern networking research. As usual, we would like to express our sincere gratitude to all those who contributed to this issue of PACMNET, especially the Authors for submitting their finest work and the Associate Editors for offering valuable feedback in their reviews and engaging in the discussions. Our thanks also go to the SIGCOMM Executive Committee Chair and the CoNEXT Steering Committee members for their continued support and guidance, providing essential suggestions and insights throughout the article selection process.

Toxic language detection for large language model safety has largely been framed as binary classification, yet unethical expressions differ in severity across types and human judgments of severity are far from uniform. We analyze a large-scale Korean ethics-verification corpus with eight type labels (seven unethical types plus neutral) and the individual intensity votes (0–3) of five raters per sentence (363,154 sentences; 1,001,030 votes). First, the seven unethical types form a three-tier perceived-severity hierarchy—censure (1.42) < discrimination, hate, and abuse (1.53–1.59) < sexual, violence and crime incitement (1.74–1.75)—supported by post-hoc tests: all between-tier differences are significant with substantial effect sizes (Holm-corrected p < 0.05; |Cliff’s δ| = 0.14–0.45), while within-tier effects are negligible. Second, automatically estimated sentiment valence barely explains the hierarchy (Spearman ρ = −0.142; AUC = 0.621; replicated with a Korean-specific sentiment model and with preceding dialogue context included in the input); the two most severe types show the most neutral surface valence, so sentiment signals capture best precisely the least severe type. Third, inter-rater agreement is low (ordinal Krippendorff’s α = 0.373), yet the disagreement is not explained by the basic demographics the corpus records—rater gender and age (equivalence tests bound the pooled gender effect at |d|≤0.013 and the age correlation at |ρ|≤0.002; unrecorded rater characteristics remain untested)—and instead grows with item severity (sentence-level ρ = 0.248). Harmfulness judgment appears to be a dimension largely independent of sentiment, whose annotation may benefit from continuous scales, multi-rater averaging, and severity-proportional rating resources.

documents.abstract: Public trust is central to the implementation of artificial intelligence (AI) in digital medicine, yet little is known about how patients respond to different forms of physician AI disclosure across clinical risk contexts. In a 5 × 2 factorial experiment in mainland China, 1574 adults were randomly assigned to physician profiles varying by AI use type and condition severity. Administrative AI was rated more favorably than diagnostic and therapeutic AI across physician perception and care-seeking intention outcomes. High-severity conditions amplified negative responses to therapeutic AI, whereas explicit non-AI disclosure was associated with greater appointment willingness under high severity. Exploratory mediation analyses suggested that competence, trust, and empathy accounted for different disclosure-related response patterns. Main effects were directionally consistent in a supplementary offline community sample from Macao ( n = 128). These findings suggest that AI disclosure in digital medicine should distinguish administrative from clinical uses and be calibrated to clinical severity, while highlighting the need for preregistered replication using behavioral outcomes.

documents.abstract: Effective task and project management needs efficient task prioritization, scheduling, progress monitoring, and coordination among people, all things considered. Conventional task management systems mostly rest on manual planning and tracking, which can make it difficult for users to manage competing priorities and changing workloads. This paper introduces PlanWise, an AI-powered personal and collaborative task management system designed to support task organization, project coordination, and intelligent productivity assistance, at least in principle. A web-based interface with backend services and database management is being blended by this setup to support personal tasks and collaborative project workflows, and includes large language model-based AI assistance for daily planning, task guidance, and project intelligence, combining task-related information and deterministic processing with AI-generated explanations and recommendations. It also is stressing user control by requiring approval for AI-suggested changes before they're employed. PlanWise is built using React and Vite for the frontend and Supabase for authentication, database operations, and backend functionality, with Google Gemini API integration for AI-assisted attributes. This paper is outlining the system architecture, design methodology, implementation approach, and evaluation framework. In fact, the current implementation founds for integrating AI assistance into the personal and collaborative task management. Further testing is required for the assessment of the reliability, potency and concrete benefits of its AI-driven capabilities. documents.abstract: Generative AI is changing not only how content is created on digital content platforms but also who provides the AI used to create it. Platforms may offer generative AI using data pooled across creators, whereas creators may provide AI services based on their own content. Understanding how these provision regimes affect creators’ investment incentives and the value generated by AI is therefore important. We develop a game-theoretic model in which human-generated content competes with AI-generated content while contributing to AI learning. The results show that platform provision can induce higher human-generated content quality than creator provision when AI learning effectiveness lies within a certain range and the platform’s pooled-data advantage is limited. A stronger pooled-data advantage can make creator provision more favorable for sustaining human-generated content quality. Platform provision can nevertheless generate higher AI-generated content quality even when creator provision induces higher human-generated content quality, provided that the pooled-data advantage is sufficiently strong. We further find that AI value sharing can encourage or discourage quality investment under platform provision, while its effects on regime preferences and preference alignment depend on market conditions. Thus, the provision regime preferred by the creator need not be the one that sustains higher human-generated content quality.

OBJECTIVES First responders often work in unpredictable, uncontrolled environments, where exposure to infected patients and contaminated environments heighten the risk of communicable disease transmission. Their higher infection prevalence compared with the general population has driven the implementation of personal protective equipment, vaccination requirements, safety protocols, and infection prevention education. The aim of this systematic review and meta-analysis was to estimate the pooled prevalence of infections among first responders in the prehospital workers including paramedics, emergency medical technicians, patient transport staff, firefighters, police, and police officers.METHODS Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science and PUBMED/Medline were systematically searched. Pooled prevalence estimates were calculated using random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood estimation, with Freeman–Tukey double-arcsine transformation and back-transformation to the original prevalence scale. Heterogeneity was assessed using I², τ², and 95% prediction intervals. Meta-regression was used to examine potential sources of between-study heterogeneity, and small-study effects and potential publication bias were assessed using funnel plots and Egger’s regression test. Risk of bias was investigated using the AXIS tool.RESULTS Following the initial search, 34,874 articles were identified, of which 88 were full-text screened. Of these, 22 studies representing 19,188 first responders were included in this systematic review. The pooled prevalences of hepatitis B and C were 6.2% (95% CI 4.5%-8.2%) and 1.8% (95% CI 0.9%-2.9%), respectively. Around 4% (95% CI 2.6%- 5.9%) of the first responders had MRSA colonisation. Current or past infection with COVID-19 among non-vaccinated first responders was 13.6% (95% CI 4.8%- 25.9%), which reduced to 7.3% (95% CI 3.6%- 12%) after exclusion of studies with high risk of bias. Of the known study characteristics, geographic region significantly contributed to heterogeneity, explaining 36.7% of between-study variance, p = 0.039.CONCLUSIONS Infectious disease prevalence varied across pathogens, occupations, and geographical settings among first responders. These findings should be interpreted in light of substantial heterogeneity and limitations in the available evidence but may help inform infection prevention, occupational health policy, vaccination strategies, and future research in first responder services.

documents.abstract: The increasing global population has intensified the demand for food, placing significant pressure on agricultural systems to enhance productivity while ensuring environmental sustainability. This review examines the integration of the Internet of Things (IoT), artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) in digital crop management, drawing on the technologies and applications discussed in the manuscript. Precision agriculture has emerged as an effective approach for optimising resource use by managing spatial and temporal variability within fields. It integrates advanced technologies such as the Global Positioning System, Geographic Information Systems, variable-rate technology, auto-steer guidance systems, wireless telematics, remote sensing, artificial intelligence and yield monitoring systems to support site-specific crop management. The adoption of the Internet of Things has further strengthened precision agriculture by enabling real-time monitoring of soil, crop and environmental parameters through sensor networks. These sensors generate continuous field data that facilitate informed decision-making and efficient resource utilisation. Furthermore, the large volume of data produced by IoT-based systems can be effectively analysed using machine learning techniques. As a subset of AI, ML enables the identification of patterns and generation of predictive insights for applications such as crop yield prediction, irrigation scheduling, nutrient management and weed detection, thereby enhancing productivity and sustainability in modern agriculture.

HT9 and Gr.92 (Mod) steels are promising candidates for advanced nuclear fuel cladding. In this study, 1,590 tensile test data points of 9–12Cr ferritic/martensitic (FM) steels were collected to develop machine learning (ML) models for predicting irradiation-induced changes in the tensile properties of HT9 and Gr.92 (Mod). Regression models were evaluated after Optuna-based hyperparameter optimization using test-set evaluation and k -fold cross-validation (CV). Extreme gradient boosting (XGB) exhibited the best predictive performance; however, an artificial neural network (ANN) was selected for its continuous response, physical consistency, and stable representation of irradiation-dependent trends. Using independent experimental data, the ANN yielded mean absolute percentage errors (MAPEs) of 6.26 ± 0.47% for ultimate tensile strength (UTS) and 10.69 ± 0.46% for yield strength (YS). The ANN model predicted the YS across irradiation conditions and showed that the irradiation-induced increase in YS for HT9 and Gr.92 (Mod) steels saturated at 5–10 displacements per atom (dpa). SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), an explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) method, quantified the contributions of dpa and irradiation temperature, revealing that irradiation temperature has a greater overall influence on the predicted YS. These results provide both reliable property predictions and physical insights into the effects of irradiation conditions.

Aims: To assess the prevalence of musculoskeletal disorders among shrimp farm workers and examine their association with selected demographic characteristics. Study Design: A descriptive research design was adopted for the study. Place and Duration of Study: The study was conducted between 2023–2026 in the selected shrimp farming areas of Andhra Pradesh (Kakinada, West Godavari and Bapatla districts) and Telangana (Narayanpet, Jogulamba Gadwal and Wanaparthy districts). Methodology: A total of 150 shrimp farm workers were selected through purposive sampling based on their involvement in shrimp-farming activities. Data were collected using a researcher-developed structured interview schedule covering demographic and occupational characteristics and self-reported musculoskeletal disorders across different body regions. Frequencies, percentages, the Wilcoxon signed-rank test and correlation analysis were used for statistical analysis. Results: Among the participants, 93.33 per cent were male and 68.67 per cent were engaged in elementary occupations. Upper back pain was frequently reported by 47.33 per cent of workers on the right side and 20 per cent on the left side. The corresponding percentages for lower back pain were 46 and 24 per cent, respectively, while wrist pain was reported by 44 per cent on the right side and 41.33 per cent on the left side. Muscle cramps were reported as occurring sometimes by 59.33 per cent on the right side and 55.33 per cent on the left side. Right-sided symptom scores were higher than left-sided scores, with a statistically significant difference between the two sides (Wilcoxon signed-rank test: Z = −8.686, p < 0.001). A statistically significant difference was observed in overall musculoskeletal discomfort scores across the occupational groups (Kruskal–Wallis H = 7.163, df = 2, p = 0.028). Pearson’s correlation analysis showed no statistically significant relationships between overall MSD scores and age, education, socioeconomic status or monthly income (p > 0.05). Conclusion: The study highlighted the occurrence of musculoskeletal disorders (MSDs) among shrimp farm workers and the need for attention to their occupational health. The findings provided a basis for identifying work-related ergonomic problems and developing suitable interventions, worker awareness programmes and regular health assessments to improve occupational health and safety in shrimp farming.

documents.abstract: This paper explores the role of Large Language Models (LLMs) in promoting sustainable behavior, specifically in overcoming procrastination. Despite widespread recognition of the need for sustainable behavior change, individuals often struggle to break free from entrenched, unsustainable habits. LLMs, such as OpenAI’s GPT-4, represent a significant breakthrough in artificial intelligence and are increasingly used in behavior change interventions. This study introduces ProactiMate, a chatbot built using Motivational Interviewing (MI) principles and a Chain of Models approach for prompt engineering, designed to help users combat procrastination. Our research compares four LLMs (GPT-3.5 Turbo, LLaMA-3.2, Qwen-2.5, and SmolLM-1.7B) for output influence on procrastination avoidance, and assesses the impact of hyperparameters (temperature and top-p values) on procrastination avoidance. The findings reveal that GPT-3.5 outperforms other models across various evaluation metrics, and higher temperature and top-p values lead to more effective procrastination avoidance from automatic evaluation. According to expert evaluations, Qwen-2.5 and GPT-3.5 Turbo demonstrated notable effectiveness in fostering user engagement and motivation for addressing procrastination, with GPT-3.5 Turbo particularly distinguished by its capacity to provide strategies that help maintain long-term motivation. And GPT’s output aligns well with both automatic evaluation metrics and human evaluation. The results provide insights into the most effective ways to use LLMs in chatbot design, offering solutions for future usability testing.

Tadqiqotda inson omilini kamaytirish, takrorlanuvchi ish hajmini qisqartirish, shuningdek, protsessual va umumiy murojaatlar oʻrtasidagi huquqiy nomuvofiqliklarni hal etish masalalari yoritilgan. Rama pojęciowa, narzędzie pomiaru i program badawczy“, wraz z aneksami nr 1 i nr 2, wynikiem rozpoznania zbiorów oraz audytem katalogów zmiennych programu HFCS. Zadanie przewidywało częściowy i zastępczy test dwóch hipotez rdzeniowych — H-C o miskalibracji kompetencji oraz H-E o spójności międzypoziomowej — na danych panelowych pochodzących ze zbiorów istniejących. Protokół określa zmienne wymagane, zbiory do sprawdzenia i regułę rozstrzygania przed przystąpieniem do rozpoznania. Rozpoznanie zamknięto wynikiem negatywnym w zakresie krajowym.
